subject.title: Agent can promise a later follow-up without starting any actual follow-up action

question: Should OpenClaw broaden the reminder guard into a same-turn future-commitment gate, and should unbacked final replies be rewritten, annotated, blocked, or forced to schedule work?
rationale: The source-backed gap is real, but choosing broad natural-language detection and mutating user-visible final replies is product policy rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Define Broad Gate First
options.body: Approve the detector scope and enforcement behavior, then implement the reply-pipeline invariant with regression tests across cron, sessions, queued follow-up, and commitments.

options.title: Keep Current Mitigations
options.body: Leave the reminder note and opt-in commitments as the only behavior, accepting that broader promise-style replies can still be unbacked.

options.title: Make Strict Mode Explicit
options.body: Add a narrowly scoped opt-in strict mode only if maintainers decide the default false-positive risk is too high.

recommendation.title: Define Broad Gate First
recommendation.body: Approve the detector scope and enforcement behavior, then implement the reply-pipeline invariant with regression tests across cron, sessions, queued follow-up, and commitments.

likelyOwner.reason: vignesh07 authored both adjacent mechanisms that the broader invariant would extend or replace.
